[Note: This sentence is absent from Arg., Basel, and Ivo; “obtains” (*impetrat*): Ivo and Basel.]

But if someone perhaps does not wish to believe what I have related concerning those endangered by imminent shipwreck—for this is commended by report from an uncertain author, not by the authority of the divine Scriptures—I shall not dispute, but shall ask [Note: “I ask” (*interrogo*): Ivo and the same edition.] what is to happen if something of this kind occurs. For no one can say that a person who desires baptism when death threatens ought to be abandoned. [Note: “that person”: absent from Arg.]

Whoever does not believe that it has happened that someone was baptized by a penitent [Note: “believe” (*credat*): collected editions except the first Basel; their text reads, “whoever does not believe that someone baptized by a penitent…,” while Arg. reads, “one who requests baptism from a penitent. Whoever…”.] ought to believe that it can happen. [Col. 1808C]

### Chapter XXXVII. However uprightly a catechumen lives, without baptism he cannot be saved.

The same, to the same person. [Note: From the book *On Ecclesiastical Dogmas*, wrongly attributed to Augustine; Burchard, book 4, chapter 16; Ivo, *Panormia*, book 1, chapter 107 and following; *Decretum*, part 1, chapter 211—all from Augustine’s sayings; *Polycarpus*, book 3, title 10; Peter Lombard, book 4, distinction 4.]

We do not believe that a catechumen, though he dies in good works, possesses eternal life, [Note: “eternal” absent from Burchard and Ivo.] except in martyrdom, in which the whole sacrament of baptism is completed. [Note: “Except” has been corrected from the original and from the Master. Earlier the text read: “except only [thus the collected editions; ‘martyrdom’: Ivo, *Panormia*; ‘completes the sacraments’: Burchard], unless martyrdom completes the sacraments.”] [Col. 1809A]

The person to be baptized [Note: “about to be baptized” (*baptizaturus*): Basel, Paris, Lyons I; “baptized” (*baptizatus*): remaining editions, Burchard, Ivo.] confesses his faith before the priest and, when questioned, answers. The martyr does this also [Note: “the same thing” (*idem*): Ivo and collected editions.] before the persecutor: he confesses his own faith [Note: “his own” absent from Burchard and Ivo.] and, when questioned, answers. [Note: “did” (*fecit*): the same editions except Lyons II, III.]

The former [Note: “and the former” (*et ille*): collected editions.] after confession is sprinkled with water, or immersed; [Note: “or immersed,” and the following *or*: omitted by Ivo; Burchard’s passage is corrupt: “the former after confession [is] sprinkled with martyrdom, or truly sprinkled with blood or tongue [of] fire.”] the latter [Note: “but the latter” (*hic vero*): Ivo and collected editions.] is sprinkled with blood or touched by fire. The former receives the Holy Spirit by the bishop’s laying on of hands; [Note: “through laying on of hands”: Basel.] the latter becomes a dwelling-place of the Holy Spirit, because it is not he himself who speaks, but the Spirit of the Father [Note: “Holy”: Ivo and collected editions.] who speaks in him.

The former partakes of the Eucharist in commemoration of the Lord’s death; [Note: “in commemoration” (*commemoratione*): the same editions except Lyons II, III; Burchard and Ivo.] the latter dies with Christ himself. The former professes that he will renounce worldly acts; [Note: “to renounce”: Ivo and collected editions.] the latter renounces life itself. [Note: “them” (*ipsis*): collected editions; “enticements” (*illecebris*) added: Basel, Lyons II, III; “renounced” (*renunciavit*): Burchard.] All sins are remitted to the former; [Note: “forgiven” (*dimittuntur*): Ivo, *Panormia*, and Basel.] in the latter they are extinguished. [Note: “in the latter” (*isti*): Burchard, Ivo, and collected editions.] [Col. 1809B]

### Chapter XXXVIII. Baptism is not repeated when its form has certainly been conferred intact.

Likewise, Pope Leo, Letter XC, alternatively XCII, to Rusticus, chapter 16. [Note: Letter 167, written A.D. 458 or 459, Ballerini edition; Burchard, book 4, chapter 42; Anselm, book 9, chapter 6 [16]; Ivo, *Panormia*, book 1, chapter 91; *Decretum*, part 1, chapter 236; *Polycarpus*, there.]

### Part VIII

Those of whom you have written, who know that they have been baptized [Note: “themselves” (*se*): Hispanic Collection; Ballerini; Burchard; Anselm; Ivo.] but profess that they do not know what faith was held by those who baptized them, however [Note: “because, however” (*quoniam quol.*): Hispanic Collection, Burchard, Ivo; “whence, because, however many” (*unde quon. quot.*): Ballerini, Anselm.] they received the form of baptism, [Note: “received” (*acceperunt*): Hispanic Collection; Ballerini; Anselm; Burchard; Ivo; collected editions.] are not to be rebaptized. [Note: “baptized” (*baptizandi*): Ballerini; Burchard; Anselm.] Rather, through the laying on of hands, invoking the power of the Holy Spirit, [Note: “invoking” (*invocata*): absent from the Hispanic Collection, Burchard, Anselm, and Ivo; Ivo: “receiving the power of the Holy Spirit, which…”] which they could not receive from heretics, they are to be joined to Catholics.

[Col. 1809C]

### Chapter XXXIX. Christ baptizes equally through good and bad ministers.

Likewise, Augustine, *Homilies on John*, tractate V, on chapter 1. [Note: Peter Lombard, book 4, distinction 5.]

### Part IX

To baptize through ministry is one thing; to baptize through power is another. [Note: “Through power”: here Augustine follows with the chapter *Baptism*, cited above under the same heading.]

And below:

§1. Therefore his disciples were baptizing, and Judas was still among his disciples. [Col. 1810A] If, then, those whom Judas baptized were not baptized again, while those whom John baptized were baptized again—were they? [Note: “but those whom he baptized”: collected editions.] Certainly they were baptized again, but it was not the same baptism. [Note: “with a repeated baptism”: collected editions.] For John baptized those whom John baptized; [Note: “and John”: Lyons II, III.] but Christ baptized those whom Judas baptized.

Likewise, tractate 6:

§2. By this power, which Christ alone retained for himself and transferred to none of his ministers, although he deigned to baptize through his ministers, [Note: “he says” added: Arg.; “I say”: remaining editions.] the unity of the Church stands, signified by the dove of which it was said: “My dove is one; she is the chosen one of her mother.” [Note: Song of Songs 6:8; “is” added: collected editions; “to her mother” (*matri*): Lyons I.]

For if, as I have already said, my brothers, [Note: “my brothers”: absent from Arg.] that power were transferred from the Lord to the minister, there would be as many baptisms as there are ministers, and the unity of baptism would no longer stand. [Col. 1810B]

Pay attention, brothers. Before our Lord Jesus Christ came to baptism, the dove descended into the water. [Note: “the Holy Spirit into”: added by Arg. and Basel. The whole passage, which caused difficulty to the author of the gloss, is corrupt. The original reads: “Before our Lord Jesus Christ had come to baptism—for after baptism the dove descended—in which John recognized something peculiar, when it was said to him: ‘He upon whom you see the Spirit descending like a dove and remaining upon him, he is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’ He knew that he himself…”] John recognized in it something peculiar to him of whom this was said: [Note: “in which John recognized something peculiar”: Arg.; John 1:33.] “He upon whom you see the Spirit descending like a dove and remaining upon him, he is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.”

He knew, [Note: “however” added: collected editions.] that he baptized in the Holy Spirit, [Note: this clause is absent from Bohm.] but he learned there that it was his own distinctive property that power should not pass from him to another, though he bestowed it. [Note: “God” (*Deo*), for “him” (*eo*): Arg. and Basel.]

Likewise, tractate 80:

§3. “You are now clean because of the word which I have spoken to you.” [Note: John 15:3; “of God” added: Basel, Lyons II, III.] Why did he not say, “You are clean because of the baptism by which you have been washed,” [Note: “cleansed” (*abluti*): collected editions.] but, “because of the word which I have spoken to you,” unless because the word cleanses even in water? [Col. 1810C] [Note: In Augustine, the chapter *Remove*, cited above under question 1, chapter 1, follows these words.]

Likewise, tractate 5:

§4. If the minister is righteous, I count him with Paul; I count him with Peter; with these I count righteous ministers. [Note: “him” (*eum*): collected editions.] But righteous ministers do not seek their own glory—for they are ministers—and do not wish to be thought leaders; [Note: “judges” (*judicibus*): original.] they are ashamed that hope should be placed in themselves. [Col. 1811A]

Therefore I count a righteous minister with Paul. For what does Paul say? [Note: “the Apostle”: Arg. and Basel; cf. 1 Corinthians 3:6.] “I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase.”

### Chapter XL. Schismatics lose neither baptism nor the power of baptizing.

The same, book I, *On Baptism against the Donatists*, chapter 1. [Note: Anselm, book 9, chapter 27 [39, 26, 46]; *Polycarpus*, book 3, title 10.]

But none of them denies that apostates also possess baptism; and when they return and are converted through penance, because it is not restored to them, [Note: “because it is lost”: collected editions.] it is judged that they could not have lost it.

Likewise, those who depart from the communion of the Church through the sacrilege of schism certainly have the baptism which they had received before departing. [Note: “in,” for “through”: collected editions; “receive”: Arg.; “had received”: Lyons II, III.] [Col. 1811B] For if they return, [Note: “return”: Arg. and Basel.] it is not given to them again. Hence it is shown that what they received while established in unity [Note: “received”: collected editions.] could not be lost when separated from unity.

But if it can be possessed outside, why cannot it also be conferred outside? If you say, “It is not rightly conferred outside,” we reply: just as it is not rightly possessed outside, yet is possessed, so it is not rightly conferred outside, yet is conferred. And just as, through reconciliation to unity, that begins to be possessed beneficially which had been possessed uselessly outside unity, so through that same reconciliation, that begins to be beneficial which had been conferred uselessly outside it.

Likewise, book 3, chapter 19:

§1. Heretics possess sacraments and Scriptures for hope, not for salvation. [Note: This is also the reading cited in *Polycarpus*. In Augustine at the place indicated occurs: “That their error may be called truth and their crime thought justice on account of the sacraments and Scriptures which they possess for appearance, not for salvation.”]

Likewise, book 4, chapter 11:

§2. An unbelieving and blasphemous person, if he persists in unbelief and blasphemy, [Note: “remains” (*remanserit*): Arg. and Basel.] receives no remission of sins either outside the Church or within the Church. [Note: “through baptism conferred,” or “through baptism,” added by the editions; “will have received”: Nor., Venice I, Paris, Lyons I.] Or, if, by the force of the sacrament, he receives it for a moment of time, [Note: “receives” (*excipit*): collected editions.] the same force operates outside and inside alike, [Note: “that force”: the same editions.] just as the power of Christ’s name also effected the expulsion of demons outside. [Note: cf. Matthew 8.] [Col. 1811C]

[Col. 1812A]

### Chapter XLI. The wicked administer baptism not by their own power but by Christ’s power.

Likewise, in the same work, book V, chapter 20. [Note: This chapter has been composed from Blessed Augustine’s words, gathered from various places and differently arranged, sometimes reduced to an epitome.] [Note: Anselm, book 9, chapter 38 [50]; *Polycarpus*, there.]

How does God hear a murderer praying [Note: “heard” (*exaudivit*): Arg., Basel, Venice II.] over baptismal water, or over oil, or over the Eucharist, or over the heads of those on whom hands are laid? Yet all these things are done and effective even through murderers—that is, [Note: “or” (*aut*): collected editions except Arg.] through those who hate their brothers. [Note: cf. 1 John 3:15.]

Even within the Church itself, since no one can give what he does not have, how does a murderer give the Holy Spirit? Yet he too baptizes within it. Therefore God gives the Holy Spirit even through that murderer baptizing. [Note: “in the one baptizing”: Basel; “in the baptism itself”: remaining editions except Lyons II, III.]

Accordingly, God gives the sacrament of grace even through the wicked; but grace itself only through himself or through his saints. [Col. 1812B] Therefore he grants remission of sins either through himself or through the members of that dove, to whom he says: “If you forgive anyone’s sins, they are forgiven him; and if you retain anyone’s sins, they shall be retained.” [Note: John 20:23; “are forgiven”: Basel; “have been retained”: the remaining editions except Arg.; Anselm omits “and if… retained.”] [Note: “his own” (*ipsius*), for “that dove’s” (*illius*): Arg., Basel, Lyons II, III.]

But if laying on of hands were not applied to one coming from heresy, [Note: “is applied” (*adhibetur*): Arg. and Basel.] he would, as it were, be judged free from every fault. [Note: The original reads: “As though he were judged free from every fault. But because of the joining of charity, etc.” Anselm: “thus” (*ita*). The text has not been corrected because of the gloss on the word “fault.”] Yet hands are laid upon corrected heretics because of the union of charity—which is the greatest gift of the Holy Spirit, without which whatever other holy things there may be in a person cannot avail for salvation. [Note: “which” (*quae*): collected editions.]

People put on Christ sometimes as far as receiving the sacrament, [Note: “Christ himself” added: collected editions except the first Basel and Lyons II, III.] sometimes also [Note: “also” added: Basel, Lyons II, III.] as far as sanctification of life. The former may be common to good and bad alike; [Col. 1812C] the latter is peculiar to good and devout persons.

§2. The reason why certain men, even eminent bishops of Christ, [Note: “and bishops”: Basel, Lyons II, III.] among whom Blessed Cyprian was especially outstanding, thought that Christ’s baptism could not exist among heretics or schismatics was only that the sacrament was not distinguished from the effect or use of the sacrament. [Note: “they did not distinguish”: collected editions.] Since its effect and use, in liberation from sins and uprightness of heart, were not found among heretics, [Col. 1813A] they thought that the sacrament itself was not there. [Note: “the effect and use of that sacrament”: collected editions; “they found”: the same editions.]

But when they turned their eyes toward the multitude of inward chaff—since those who are perverse and live ruinously even within unity plainly can neither confer nor possess remission of sins, because it was said not to wicked but to good children, “If you forgive anyone’s sins, they are forgiven him; if you retain anyone’s sins, they shall be retained,” [Note: “they are forgiven them,” and the remaining variants: collected editions; “and if… retained”: absent from Anselm; cf. John 20:23.] while nevertheless they possess, confer, and receive the sacrament of baptism—it became sufficiently clear to the shepherds of the Catholic Church that the sheep wandering outside and receiving the Lord’s mark outside, when it came to the salvation of Christian unity, should be corrected from error; but that the Lord’s mark on it should be recognized rather than rejected. [Note: “known” (*cognosci*): collected editions.]

For many wolves both possess that mark and impress it on wolves; they indeed appear to be within, but do not belong to that one sheep which is one even out of many. [Note: “outside” omitted: Bohm; “belongs”: collected editions except the first Basel and Lyons II, III; “also”: in the phrase “which also is one out of many,” as printed.]

§3. When a bad person confers baptism on a good person—that is, on one changed by true conversion within the bond of unity—the wickedness of the giver does not separate the good sacrament which is conferred from the good believer to whom it is conferred. [Note: “the wickedness is overcome”: the true reading, preserved by Anselm.]

And when sins are forgiven to one truly converted to God, by those to whom he is joined by that same true confession, the Holy Spirit forgives them—the Spirit given to all saints cleaving to him in charity, whether they know one another bodily or do not know one another. [Note: *ipse* (“he himself”): collected editions, for *ipsa* (“the same [confession]”).]

Likewise, when someone’s sins are retained, they are certainly retained by those from whom he is separated by perversity of heart, whether known bodily or unknown. [Col. 1813C]

§4. All wicked persons are spiritually separated from the good. [Note: “specially” (*specialiter*): Basel.] But if they are also bodily separated by open dissension, they become worse. [Note: “are worse”: Basel.] Yet it makes no difference to the holiness of baptism how much worse is the person who possesses it, or to how much worse a person he confers it. [Note: “to a worse person” added: Basel, Lyons II, III.] A separated person can confer it, just as he can possess it. But as it is ruinous to possess it, so it is ruinous to confer it. The person to whom it is conferred [Note: “who confers it”: original; “who conferred it”: collected editions except Lyons II, III.] can receive it beneficially if he himself receives it while not separated, under pressure of the necessity of death.

§5. Why can heretics not baptize outside? Is it because they are worse precisely because they are outside? But it makes no difference to the integrity of baptism how much worse is the person who confers it. [Note: “conferred or gives it”: Arg.] [Col. 1814A] For the difference between a bad person and a worse person is not as great as the difference between a good person and a bad person; yet when a bad person baptizes, he gives nothing other than what a good person gives. Therefore, when a worse person baptizes, he gives nothing other than the one who is less bad gives.

Or perhaps it belongs not to a person’s merit but to the sacrament of baptism itself that it cannot be conferred outside. If so, neither could it be possessed outside, and one would have to be baptized as often as a person, departing from the Church, returned again to the Church.

§6. For those baptized with a false heart, [Note: From this point through “Now, forgiven sins return,” the passage is an epitome of words of Blessed Augustine, spoken partly in the person of the Donatists and partly in his own person.] either sins are not forgiven at all, because the Holy Spirit of discipline flees from the false person, [Note: “Holy” added: Arg. and Basel.] or, at the very moment of time, they are forgiven through the force of the sacrament and are afterward reimposed through falseness. Thus both this is true: “As many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ,” [Note: Galatians 3:27; “Christ,” after *baptized into*, absent from Basel.] [Col. 1814B] and this: “For the Holy Spirit of discipline flees from the false person.” [Note: Wisdom 1:5; “For the Holy Spirit” absent from Arg. and Basel.]

That is, the holiness of baptism clothes him with Christ, [Note: *Christum* (“Christ”): collected editions, for *Christo* (“with Christ”).] and the ruin of falseness strips him of Christ. [Note: *Christum* (“Christ”): collected editions, for *Christo* (“of Christ”).]

For the Lord teaches most plainly in the Gospel that forgiven sins return where fraternal charity is absent, in the case of the servant from whom the lord demanded the debt he had forgiven, because that servant would not forgive his fellow servant’s debt.

Thus baptismal grace is not prevented from forgiving all sins, even if fraternal hatred persists in the mind of the person whose sins are forgiven. The preceding day is released, and whatever remains is released, even in the hour and moment before baptism and in baptism itself. [Note: “moment” (*momentum*): original, Anselm, Ivo; “in baptism itself”: collected editions except Arg.] Thereafter, however, he immediately begins to be guilty not only of subsequent days but also of past days, hours, and moments, because all the sins which had been forgiven return. [Note: “sins”: absent from Ivo.] [Col. 1814C]

### Chapter XLII. When baptism benefits one who received it falsely.

The same, in the same first book *On Baptism*, and the same chapter 12. [Note: Cf. above, end of chapter 32.]

### Part X

Baptism begins to avail for salvation when that falseness has departed through true confession—the falseness which, while the heart persisted in wickedness or sacrilege, did not permit the abolition of sins [Note: “absolution” (*absolutionem*): collected editions.] to occur.

### Chapter XLIII. Sacraments conferred outside the Church are not repeated.

The same, Letter XLVIII to the Donatists. [Note: Letter 113, written A.D. 408, Maurist edition; *Polycarpus*, book 3, title 10.]

We do not alter in you those respects in which you are with us [Col. 1815A] (for in many respects you are with us); for of such persons it was also said: “For in many things they were with me” [Ps. 54:19]. But we correct those respects in which you are not with us, and we wish you here to receive those things which you do not possess there, where you are. You are with us in baptism, in the Creed, and in the other sacraments of the Lord. But in the spirit of unity and bond of peace, and indeed in the Catholic Church itself, you are not with us.

[Note: “Of the Lord and Catholic”: editions of Arg. and Bas.]

And in Epistle 51, to Boniface [Note: Ep. 185 (written A.D. 417), Maurist edition], §1: But those with whom we deal, or concerning whom we deal, are not to be despaired of, for they are still in the body; but let them not seek the Holy Spirit except in the body of Christ. They possess outwardly the sacrament of that body, but do not inwardly possess the reality of which that sacrament is the sacrament; and therefore they eat and drink judgment upon themselves.

[Col. 1815B]

### C. XLIV. How those baptized among heretics in the name of the Trinity are to be received by the Church

Likewise, Gregory to Quirinus, Bishop, and the other bishops in Iberia, Book IX, Epistle 61.

[Note: *Iberia*: thus corrected from the original Vatican manuscript. Previously it read *Hibernia* [so the editions compared with the original].]

[Note: Ep. 67 (written A.D. 601), Book 11, Maurist edition.—Anselm, Book 8, c. 24. Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 88 (as far as “is reformed”); *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 153; *Polycarpus*, same place.]

We have learned from the ancient institution of the Fathers that those baptized among heretics in the name of the Trinity, when they return to the holy Church, are to be recalled to the bosom of Mother Church either by anointing with chrism, by laying on of hands, or by profession of faith alone.

[Note: “shall have returned”: editions of Arg. and Bas.]

Thus the West restores Arians to entrance into the holy Catholic Church by laying on of hands, whereas the East does so by anointing with holy chrism. But it receives Monothelites and others by a true confession alone, because the holy baptism which they received among heretics then receives in them the power of cleansing, when either the former receive the Holy Spirit through laying on of hands, or the latter are united to the bosom of the holy and universal Church by their profession of the true faith.

[Note: *Monothelites*: in the original, in Polycarpus, and in Ivo’s text, the reading is *Monophysites*. John Damascene writes of this heresy in his book *On the Two Wills of Christ*, as do Nicephorus and others. But the text has not been changed because of the gloss.]

[Note: “Monuscelites”: Nor. edition.—“Monoschelites”: Lugdd. II and III.—“Monoscelites”: remaining editions.]

[Note: “which is among heretics, are”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: “cleansing”: “correction,” same edition.]

[Note: “receives”: Ivo; Arg. edition.—“received”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: “received”: same edition.]

[Note: “were”: editions compared with the original, Bas.]

### C. XLV. Baptism can be received outside the Church, but does not profit there

Likewise, Augustine, *On Baptism*, c. 1.

[Note: This chapter has been enlarged from the original, so that its meaning may be understood more clearly.]

The Church, compared with Paradise, shows us that people may indeed receive her baptism even outside her [Col. 1816A], but that no one can either obtain or retain the blessedness of salvation outside her.

[Note: “receive”: editions compared with the original.]

[Note: Addition, “the Church”: editions of Bas., Lugdd. II and III.]

“For the rivers flowing from the fountain of Paradise, as Scripture testifies [cf. Gen. 2], also flowed forth abundantly outside it. They are expressly named, together with the lands through which they flow. And it is known to all that they are situated outside Paradise.” Yet there is not in Mesopotamia, or in Egypt, whither those rivers reached, that happiness of life which is spoken of in Paradise.

[Note: “But not”: editions compared with the original.]

[Note: “in”: editions compared with the original.]

[Note: “reach”: Arg. edition.]

“Thus it comes about that, although the water of Paradise is outside Paradise, blessedness nevertheless is not outside Paradise.” Therefore the baptism of the Church may exist outside the Church, but the gift of blessed life is found only within the Church.

[Note: “good”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: “is found”: editions compared with the original, Bas.]

[Col. 1816B]

### C. XLVI. The heresy and sacrilege of heretics are not sacraments

Likewise, *On the One Baptism against the Donatists*, Book III, c. 11.

[Note: *Heresy*: thus corrected from several old copies. Previously it read: “The baptism and sacrilege of heretics are not sacraments.”]

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 32; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 164.]

But baptism, which is Christ’s, ought not to be called theirs in the same manner as their heresy is theirs, their error is theirs, and the sacrilege of their separation is theirs.

[Note: “But not as”: original; Ivo.]

[Note: Omitted in Bas. edition.]

[Note: “secession”: same edition.]

[Note: “their”: editions compared with the original.]

[Note: “ought not”: the same editions, except Arg.]

### C. XLVII. On the same subject

Likewise, Book V, c. 13.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 33; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 167.]

Since baptism given through a contemptible man has as much force as baptism given through an apostle, it is recognized as belonging neither to the one nor to the other, but to Christ.

[Note: “the latter”: Lugdd. II and III.]

[Note: “the latter”: Ivo, *Panormia*.—“nor to the one”: absent from the editions of Nor., Ven. I and II, Par., Lugd. I, and Böhm.]

Likewise, c. 14, §1: We find “my glory,” though certainly in the Lord, and “my ministry,” “my wisdom,” and “my Gospel,” though certainly bestowed and given by the Lord, to have been said by the Apostle; but none of them ever at all said, “my baptism.”

[Note: “apostles”: Ivo, *Panormia*; editions compared with the original.]

[Note: Addition, “be”: editions of Bas., Lugdd. II and III.]

[Note: “my baptism … mine”: Ivo; editions compared with the original.]

For grace is not equal in all, nor do all minister equally; nor are all endowed with equal wisdom, and in preaching the Gospel one works better than another. Therefore one person may be called more learned than another in the doctrine of salvation itself; but one person cannot be called more or less baptized than another, whether baptized by one inferior or by one greater.

[Note: “glory”: original; Ivo; editions compared with the original except Bas., Lugdd. II and III.]

[Note: Addition, “knowledge”: Par. edition.—“or holiness or knowledge”: Arg. edition.—“or knowledge”: the remaining editions.]

[Col. 1817A]

### C. XLVIII. On the same subject

Likewise, Book IV, c. 15.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 34; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 165.]

We have sufficiently shown that, in relation to baptism consecrated by the words of the Gospel, the error of either giver or recipient is irrelevant, even if he thinks otherwise concerning the Father, or the Father, or the Son, or the Holy Spirit, than heavenly teaching declares.

### C. XLIX. The sacraments of the Church are common to good and bad alike

Likewise, in the book *On Baptism*.

[Note: The substance of this chapter as far as the words “Thus there are” occurs in the book *On the One Baptism against Petilian*, cc. 14 and 15.]

There is a unity of the Church, extending widely in the fellowship and communion of the sacraments, which embraces chaff together with grain [cf. Matt. 3:12], when it so endures their bodily mixture that the righteous neither avoid them nor are avoided by them. Thus there are evil persons in the Church [Col. 1817B], just as there are evil humours in the human body, which sometimes leave the body.

[Note: “Thus there are”: the saying is taken from Blessed Augustine on the First Epistle of John and from Bede on the same passage; but the ordinary gloss there reads: “False persons are in the Church as bad humours are in the body; when they are vomited out, the body is relieved; so, when the wicked depart, the Church is relieved.”]

### C. L. The wickedness of the person blessing does not pass into the water of baptism

Likewise, *On the One Baptism against the Donatists*, Book III, c. 10.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 54; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 116.]

The water over which God’s name is invoked is not profane and adulterous, even if it is invoked by profane and adulterous persons; for neither the creature itself nor the Name itself is adulterous.

[Note: “persons”: Lugd. II edition.]

[Note: “and by”: editions of Bas., Lugdd. II and III.]

[Note: Addition, “is adulterous”: editions compared with the original except Arg.]

### C. LI. One baptized by heretics is not to be rebaptized

Likewise, Bede, Homily XXXVI, on John c. 3.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 85; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 173; Peter Lombard, Book 4, distinction 6.]

Whether a heretic, schismatic, or criminal person baptizes in confession of the Holy Trinity, the person thus baptized [Col. 1817C] may not be rebaptized by good Catholic believers, lest the confession or invocation of so great a Name seem to be annulled.

[Note: “true”: Bas. edition.]

### C. LII. Those baptized by pagans are to be baptized in the name of the Trinity

Likewise, Gregory II to Bishop Boniface, final epistle.

[Note: Rather Gregory III, A.D. 738 = *Collectio trium partium*, Part 1, title 57, c. 3.—Ivo, *Decretum*, Part 11, c. 91.]

Those whom you asserted had been baptized by pagans: if this is so, we command you to baptize them anew in the name of the Trinity.

[Note: “command that they be baptized”: Arg. edition.]

[Col. 1818A]

### C. LIII. No one is to be baptized without exorcisms and exsufflations

Likewise, Pope Celestine to the bishops of Gaul, Epistle I, c. 12.

[Note: Written A.D. 431.—Burchard, Book 4, c. 10; Ivo, *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 205; Polycarpus, Book 3, title 20.]

**Part XI.** Whether little children or youths come to the sacrament of regeneration, they are not to approach the font of life before the unclean spirit has been driven from them by the exorcisms and exsufflations of the clergy.

[Note: “shall have come”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: “driven away”: original; Burchard, Ivo, Nor. edition.—“driven away or cast out”: Arg. edition.]

### C. LIV. The office of catechizing must precede baptism

Likewise, Rabanus, *On the Instruction of Clerics*, Book I, c. 25.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 38; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 82 ff.; Peter Lombard, Book 4, distinction 6.]

Before baptism, the office of catechizing ought to come first for a person, so that the catechumen may first receive the rudiments of faith.

[Note: “come to a person”: original.—“come in a person”: Ivo, *Panormia*.]

Likewise in the same place, §1: Jesus [Col. 1818B] himself first smeared the eyes of the man born blind with mud made from spittle, and then sent him to the waters of Siloam [cf. John 9], because one who is to be baptized must first be instructed in faith in Christ’s incarnation and then, now believing, be admitted to baptism, so that he may know in whose grace he shares and to whom he thereafter becomes a debtor.

[Note: “whose”: Bas. edition.]

### C. LV. At what time catechumens are to be brought for exorcism

Likewise, from the Second Council of Braga, c. 1.

[Note: Held A.D. 572.—Cf. C. 10, q. 1, c. 12.—Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 39.—Cf. Burchard, Book 4, c. 8; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 203.]

Twenty days before baptism, catechumens are to assemble for the cleansing of exorcism; during these twenty days they are to be fully instructed spiritually in the Creed, namely: “I believe in God the Father almighty.”

[Note: “for the cleansing exorcism”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: “run together”: Spanish Collection; Ivo; editions compared with the original.]

[Note: “especially”: Spanish Collection; Bas. edition.]

[Col. 1818C]

Likewise, from the Council of Agde, c. 13.

[Note: Held A.D. 506.—Burchard, Book 4, c. 29; Ivo, *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 223.]

It was likewise decreed that, in all churches, on one day—that is, eight days before the Lord’s resurrection—the Creed should publicly be preached in church to those seeking baptism.

[Note: Omitted in Arg. edition.]

[Note: “seven”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: “delivered”: Spanish Collection; Burchard; Ivo.]

### C. LVII. Candidates for baptism may be catechized in every church

Likewise, Pope Nicholas.

[Note: This does not occur among the extant epistles expressly attributed to Nicholas.—Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 40; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 87, attributes it to Nicholas writing to John, Archbishop of Ravenna.]

The catechisms of those to be baptized may be performed by the priests of each individual church [Col. 1819A], just as they are shown to be solemnly performed in this holy Roman Church, to which, by God’s ordering, we render the ministry of our service.

### C. LVIII. On the same subject

Likewise, from the Council of Laodicea, c. 46.

[Note: Held between A.D. 347 and 381.—Burchard, Book 4, c. 9; Anselm, Book 9, c. 20; Ivo, *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 204, cite this from Dionysius.]

Those to be baptized must learn the Creed of faith and recite it to the bishop or presbyters on the Thursday of the final week.

[Note: *Creed of faith*: this is the ancient version [i.e. the Spanish], and conveys the sense fairly well. But here the Greek is: **τὴν πίστιν**, “the faith.”]

[Note: “presbyter”: Spanish Collection; editions compared with the original.]

Likewise, from the Council of Martin of Braga, c. 49.

[Note: Cc. 45, 46 of the Council of Laodicea, from the translation of Martin of Braga [“Pope”: editions compared with the original].]

It is not permitted to receive anyone for baptism less than two weeks before Easter, but rather three weeks before it. In these days, however, those who are to be baptized must learn the Creed and, on Thursday [Col. 1819B] of the final week, recite it to the bishop or presbyter.

[Note: “and … recite”: absent from Arg. edition.]

Likewise, from the Fourth Council of Carthage, c. 85.

[Note: C. 23, *Statuta ecclesiae antiqua*.—Cf. c. 9, Distinction 18.—Burchard, Book 4, c. 11; Ivo, *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 206.]

Those to be baptized shall give their names and, after a long period of abstinence from wine and flesh, and frequent examination by laying on of hands, shall receive baptism.

[Note: “while”: Spanish Collection.—“and for a long time”: absent from Burchard and Ivo.]

### C. LXI. Why those to be baptized are exorcized and exsufflated

Likewise, Rabanus, *On the Instruction of Clerics*, Book I, c. 27.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 41; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 90.]

After the person to be baptized has, through confession of the true faith, commended himself to the lordship of another, and through renunciation has withdrawn himself from the service of his former possessor [Col. 1819C], the cruel power is exsufflated from him, so that the fleeing evil spirit may yield to the Holy Spirit through the pious ministry of the priest.

[Note: “has commended”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: “from”: absent from editions compared with the original except Bas., Lugdd. II and III.]

[Note: “pure”: editions of Arg. and Bas.]

### C. LXII. On the same subject

Likewise, Augustine, *On the Creed*, Book I, c. 1.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 42; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 94.]

As you know, dearest brothers, even little children are exsufflated and exorcized, so that the hostile power of the devil may be expelled from them—the power which deceived the human being in order to possess human beings. Therefore it is not God’s creature in infants that is exorcized or exsufflated [Col. 1820A], but he under whom are all who are born under sin.

[Note: “dearest brothers”: absent from the original and Ivo.]

[Note: “all”: absent from Ivo.]

### C. LXIII. Why the person to be baptized is signed on heart and forehead

Likewise, Rabanus, *On the Instruction of Clerics*, Book I, c. 27.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 43; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 95.]

Afterward, the person to be baptized is signed with the sign of the holy cross both on the forehead and on the heart, so that from that time the apostate devil himself, recognizing in his former vessel the sign of his own destruction, may know that it is henceforth alien to him.

[Note: “sign”: original; Ivo; Arg. edition.]

### C. LXIV. Why prayers are said over him

Likewise, in the same place, immediately following.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 44; *Decretum*, Part 1, cc. 97, 99.]

Thereafter prayers are said over him, that he may become a catechumen. Then blessed salt is given to the person to be baptized in the mouth [Col. 1820B], so that, seasoned with the salt of wisdom through this symbolic salt, he may be free from the stench of wickedness and may no longer decay from the worms of sins, but may instead be kept unharmed for receiving greater grace.

[Note: “lest”: editions compared with the original.—“so that neither”: Ivo, *Panormia*.]

[Note: “decays”: Arg. edition.]

### C. LXV. Why catechumens are initiated with salt

Likewise, Bede on Ezra, Book II, c. 9.

[Note: Previously this was cited as being in the Books of Kings [thus Ivo and the editions compared with the original].]

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 45; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 100.]

We are commanded to offer the salt of heavenly wisdom, by which catechumens are initiated, in all the sacrifices of our works.

[Note: “is commanded to be offered”: Bas. edition.]

Likewise, Rabanus, *On the Instruction of Clerics*, Book I, c. 27.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 46; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 102.]

Thereupon the devil is exorcized again, so that, recognizing his own wickedness and fearing God’s just judgment upon himself, he may withdraw from the human being and no longer seek [Col. 1820C] by his craft to overthrow him, lest he attain baptism; but rather, rendering honour to God his Creator, may restore the work to its Maker.

[Note: “is exorcized so that”: editions of Nor., Ven. I and II.—“are exorcized so that”: the remaining editions except Arg.]

[Note: Omitted in editions of Nor., Ven. I and II.]

[Note: “presume”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: “to God the Creator”: Ivo, *Panormia*.—“to God the Maker”: *Decretum*; editions compared with the original.]

Likewise, Pope Gregory, Homily XXIX on the Gospels.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 47; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 103.]

When priests, through the grace of exorcism, lay hands on believers and forbid evil spirits to dwell in their minds [Col. 1821A], what else do they do but cast out demons?

[Note: “The priest”: Arg. edition.]

[Note: “lays on”: editions of Arg. and Bas.]

[Note: “minds”: editions compared with the original except Lugdd. II and III.]

[Note: “forbids”: editions of Arg. and Bas.]

### C. LXVIII. Why the nostrils and ears are touched with saliva

Likewise, Rabanus, *On the Instruction of Clerics*, Book I, c. 27.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 48; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 104.]

Afterward his nostrils and ears are touched with saliva, and that Gospel word is said to him which Jesus spoke when he healed the deaf and mute man, touching his tongue with spittle and putting his fingers into his ears: “Ephphatha,” that is, “Be opened.”

[Note: “with saliva”: editions compared with the original.]

[Note: Addition, “said”: the same editions except Bas.; Ivo, *Panormia*.]

[Note: “ear”: editions compared with the original; Ivo, *Panormia*.]

[Note: Mark 7:34.]

[Note: “Effata”: Böhm.]

For this sacrament is performed here so that, through the symbolic saliva and touch of the priest, divine wisdom and power may effect the salvation of that catechumen: that his nostrils may be opened to receive the fragrance of the knowledge of God, that his ears may be opened to hear God’s commands [Col. 1821B], and that his inward faculty may be opened in his inmost heart to make response.

[Note: “receive”: Ivo, *Panormia*.—“perceive”: editions of Arg. and Bas.]

[Note: “That they may be opened”: in the original and in Ivo it reads: “to hear the commands of God and to store them in the inward sense of the heart” [“in the inmost heart”: Ivo, *Panormia*].]

### C. LXIX. Why the bishop touches the nostrils, not the mouths, of those to be baptized

Likewise, Ambrose, *On the Sacraments*, Book I, c. 1.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 49; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 106.]

For the glory of the office and work, the bishop touches not the mouth but the nostrils. Why the nostrils? That you may receive the good fragrance of eternal piety.

[Note: “the grace of the work and office”: original.]

[Note: “receive”: editions of Bas., Lugdd. II and III.—“receive”: remaining editions.]

### C. LXX. Why they are anointed by the priest

Likewise, Rabanus, *On the Instruction of Clerics*, Book I, c. 27.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, cc. 50, 52; *Decretum*, Part 1, cc. 108, 110.]

Then he is anointed by the priest, so that the sacred baptism received with faith may be kept. His breast is then anointed with consecrated oil, with invocation of the Holy Trinity, so that no remnants of the hidden enemy may remain in him, but his mind may be strengthened in faith in the Holy Trinity [Col. 1821C]. He is also anointed between the shoulders with the same oil, so that he may be protected on every side and strengthened by God’s grace to perform good works. Likewise, c. 28, §1: After these things he is consecrated, and the catechumen proceeds to baptism itself.

[Note: “is protected by priestly blessing”: original.]

[Note: “are anointed”: editions of Bas., Par., and Lugdd.]

[Note: “will be anointed”: original.]

[Note: “will be anointed”: same source.]

[Note: Omitted in editions of Arg. and Bas.]

[Note: “glory”: original.]

[Note: “may be consecrated”: Ivo, *Panormia*.]

[Note: “so that … may proceed”: editions compared with the original.—“and … may proceed”: Ivo, *Panormia*.]

### C. LXXI. How the presence of the Trinity consecrates the font of baptism

Likewise, Ambrose, *On the Sacraments*, Book II, c. 5.

[Note: This chapter has in several places been compressed into almost excessive narrowness. It is therefore preferable to consult the original itself.]

[Note: Ivo, *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 111, reports the first portion.]

The priest comes to the font, says the prayer, invokes the name of the Father, the presence of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and uses heavenly words [Col. 1822A]. The heavenly words are Christ’s words. The presence of the Trinity is at hand; the eternal Word works. The Spirit descends, as a dove first descended, so that unbelievers might be called to faith. In the beginning there had to be a sign; in later times there must be perfection. For the Holy Spirit was given to the Apostles in tongues of fire because of unbelievers; but for us now, in the fullness of the Church, truth is to be apprehended not through signs but through faith.

[Note: “says a prayer at the font”: original.]

[Note: Addition, “are”: editions compared with the original.]

[Note: “and there”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: Addition, “Holy”: editions compared with the original.]

[Note: “but first”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: “must be”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: Addition, “but”: editions compared with the original.]

[Note: Omitted in Arg. edition.]

### C. LXXII. Words of error uttered through ignorance do not hinder the sanctification of the water

Likewise, Augustine, *On the One Baptism*, Book VI, c. 25.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, cc. 52, 53; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 115.]

**Part XII.** If water is not sanctified when one who offers prayer, through ignorance, pours out some erroneous words [Col. 1822B], then many brothers, not only bad but also good, do not sanctify water even in the Church itself. For the prayers of many are corrected every day if they are recited to more learned persons, and many things contrary to the Catholic faith are found in them. If it should become known that certain persons were baptized when those prayers were said over the water, will they be ordered to be baptized again? Why indeed? Because the intention of the one praying generally outweighs the defect in the prayer, and because those certain Gospel words, without which baptism cannot be consecrated, have such force that by them whatever is said against the rule of faith in a faulty prayer is so nullified, just as a demon is expelled by the name of Christ.

[Note: Omitted in editions of Arg. and Bas.]

[Note: “preacher”: editions of Ven. I and II.—“of prayers”: Par. edition.]

[Note: “poured out”: editions of Bas. and Lugd. I.]

[Note: “may become known”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: “therefore”: same edition.]

[Note: “or certainly all”: Ivo, *Panormia*.—“the rest”: editions of Arg., Nor., Ven. I and II.]

For indeed, if a heretic offers a faulty prayer and does not possess the charitable disposition by which that ignorance may be overcome—and therefore is like anyone in the Catholic Church itself who is envious [Col. 1822C] and malicious, persons such as Cyprian rebukes there—he also offers, as commonly happens, some prayer in which he speaks against the rule of faith. For many persons rush into using prayers composed not only by ignorant talkers but even by heretics, and, in the simplicity of their ignorance unable to discern that they are not good, use them believing that they are good. Yet what is perverse in those prayers does not nullify what is right in them, but is rather nullified by it.

[Note: “effect”: Arg. edition.]

[Note: Addition, “Church”: editions compared with the original; Böhm.]

[Note: “unclean or envious, or malicious”: Ivo, *Panormia*.—“is envious, unclean, or malicious”: editions compared with the original.]

[Note: “here”: the same editions; Ivo, *Panormia*.]

[Note: “them”: editions compared with the original except Lugdd. II and III.]

[Note: “judge”: Bas. edition.]

[Col. 1823A]

### C. LXXIII. What the mysteries celebrated at the font of baptism signify

Likewise, Augustine to the Newly Baptized, Homily III.

[Note: This is not Augustine’s.—Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 55; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 194.]

**Part XIII.** In the first and second instruction, therefore, we spoke only of those things which, before you came to the holy font, we delivered to you according to the institutions of the Catholic Church. We also explained, insofar as the Lord deigned to grant it, what the anointing signified which, applied to the various parts of our bodies, denotes a different meaning; showing that through the oil of sanctification you had been prepared [Col. 1823B] for hearing the fullness of faith, summoned to Christ’s good fragrance, and admonished with your whole heart to renounce the devil.

[Note: “and second”: absent from the original.]

[Note: “rule”: Ivo.]

[Note: “your”: original; Ivo, *Panormia*.]

[Note: “for judgment or for hearing”: Arg. edition.]

[Note: “and from”: editions compared with the original except Bas.]

[Note: “the devil”: Bas. edition.]

But now we are going to speak of the inner mysteries which were celebrated at the sacred font itself. For, after you had given the most solemn pledge, by which you promised to renounce all the pomps of the devil, all his works, and every diabolical fornication, you descended into the holy font, the font of redemption, a font sanctified by heavenly power. Before we immersed you bodily in this font, therefore, we asked: “Do you believe in God the Father almighty?” You replied: “I believe.” Again we asked: “Do you also believe in Jesus Christ, his Son, who was born of the Holy Spirit, of the Virgin Mary?” Each of you replied: “I believe.” Again we asked: “Do you also believe in the Holy Spirit?” You replied likewise: “I believe.”

[Note: “holy”: Ivo, *Decretum*; Bas. edition; absent from the remaining editions.]

[Note: Addition, “now”: editions of Bas., Lugdd. II and III.]

[Note: “promised”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: “you descend”: Arg. edition.—“descending”: original; Ivo.]

[Note: “font, sacred font”: original; Ivo, *Decretum*.]

[Note: The reading “who was conceived of the Holy Spirit, born of Mary” occurs in editions of Bas., Lugdd. II and III.]

[Note: “Likewise”: editions compared with the original; Ivo, *Panormia*.]

This we did in accordance with the command of our Lord Jesus Christ the Saviour, who, when he was ascending to the Father in heaven, commanded his disciples, that is, the Apostles, saying: “Go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit” [Matt. 28:19].

[Col. 1824A]

(Likewise:) §1. But when we asked, “Do you believe the holy Church, the remission of sins, the resurrection of the flesh?” we did not ask this in such a way that you should believe in the holy Catholic Church as you believe in God. For it is holy and Catholic because it rightly believes in God. Therefore we did not say that you should believe in the Church as in God; rather, understand us to say, and to have said, that while living in the holy Catholic Church you should believe in God, and should also believe in the resurrection of the flesh which is to come.

[Note: “Do you believe the holy”: it was read “in the holy.” The particle *in* [absent from editions of Arg. and Nor.] was introduced from several ancient copies and from Ivo. Augustine also frequently teaches that this is how one ought to speak.]

[Note: Omitted in editions compared with the original except Lugdd. II and III.]

[Note: Omitted in the same editions except Bas. and Lugdd.]

### C. LXXIV. Little children are baptized on another’s faith and profession

Likewise, Isidore, *On Ecclesiastical Offices*, Book II, c. 24.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 13; Peter Lombard, Book 4, distinction 6.]

**Part XIV.** Little children are baptized while another makes profession for them [Col. 1824B], because they do not yet know how to speak or believe; likewise the sick, mute, and deaf, for whom another makes profession, in order that he may answer for them while they are being baptized.

### C. LXXV. Sick persons are to be baptized on the testimony of others

Likewise, from the Third Council of Carthage, c. 34.

[Note: Held A.D. 397.—Burchard, Book 4, c. 36; Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 14; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 123.]

Sick persons, if they cannot answer for themselves, are to be baptized when their will has given testimony of itself. The same procedure is to be followed in the case of penitents.

[Note: *Their will*: nothing has been altered because of the gloss on the word “has said.” But in all ancient copies of Gratian, in the Third Council of Carthage, in the African Council in the three-volume printed collection of councils, and in Ivo, who cites Isidore, the reading is: “When they have themselves testified concerning their will” [thus the Spanish Collection; and Ivo, *Panormia*, omits the word *themselves*]. But in the same African Council, in the *Codex canonum*, in the more recent edition of the Council of Carthage, and in Burchard, it reads: “When those who attended them at their own risk have testified concerning their will.” In the Greek Council of Carthage it is: **ὅτε τῇ αὐτῶν προαιρέσει τὴν περὶ αὐτῶν μαρτυρίαν κινδύνῳ ἰδίῳ εἴπωσιν**, “when, at their own risk, they make testimony concerning their intention.”]

[Note: “are baptized”: Lugdd. II and III.]

[Note: “Likewise … is”: not in the Spanish Collection.]

[Note: “petitioners”: Arg. edition.]

### C. LXXVI. The sacrament of faith, not faith itself, makes the little child a believer

Likewise, Augustine, Epistle XXIII, to Boniface.

[Note: Ep. 98 (written A.D. 408), Maurist edition.—Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 56; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 187; Peter Lombard, same place.]

To believe is nothing other than to have faith. Accordingly, when it is answered that an infant believes, though he does not yet possess the disposition of faith [Col. 1824C], the answer is that he has faith because of the sacrament of faith, and that he turns to God because of the sacrament of conversion; for the response itself belongs to the celebration of the sacrament.

[Note: “so often it”: Bas. edition.—“the whole”: editions compared with the original except Arg.]

[Note: “effect”: Ivo, *Panormia*; editions compared with the original.]

[Note: “solemnity”: editions compared with the original.]

Likewise below [cf. below, c. 129], §1: Although the little child does not yet have that faith which consists in the will of believers, nevertheless the sacrament of faith itself makes him a believer. For, just as it is answered that he believes, so he is also called a believer—not by mentally assenting to the reality itself [Col. 1825A], but by receiving the sacrament of that reality.

[Note: “makes”: Lugdd. II and III.]

[Note: “for faithful persons are also called”: editions compared with the original.]

[Note: “dissenting”: editions of Bas. and Lugdd.]

### C. LXXVII. Another’s profession does not avail for one able to answer for himself

Likewise, *On Baptism*, Book IV, c. 24.

[Note: Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 15; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 124; Peter Lombard, same place.—Cf. above, c. 34.]

When others answer for little children, so that the celebration of the sacrament may be fulfilled in their case, it certainly avails for their consecration, because they themselves cannot answer. But if another answers for one who can answer for himself, it does not likewise avail. From this rule comes that saying in the Gospel which naturally moves everyone when it is read: “He is of age; let him speak for himself.”

[Note: “others do not”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: “that Gospel saying”: editions compared with the original; cf. John 9:21.]

[Col. 1825B]

### C. LXXVIII. Why triple immersion is performed in baptism

Likewise, Augustine, Homily III.

[Note: In the sermon *On the Mystery of Baptism*, falsely attributed to Augustine.—Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 57; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 194; Peter Lombard, Book 4, distinction 3.]

After you promised to believe, we immersed your heads three times in the sacred font. This order of baptism is performed with a twofold signification of mystery. You were rightly immersed three times, because you received baptism in the name of the Holy Trinity. You were rightly immersed three times, because you received baptism in the name of Jesus Christ, who rose from the dead on the third day. For that thrice-repeated immersion represents the type of the Lord’s burial, through which you were buried with Christ in baptism and rose with Christ in faith, so that, washed from sins, you might live in holiness of virtues, imitating Christ.

[Note: “three times”: Arg. edition.]

[Note: “signification”: Bas. edition.]

[Note: “Rightly … Trinity”: absent from Arg. edition.]

[Note: “absolved”: editions compared with the original.]

[Note: “put on”: Arg. edition.]

### C. LXXIX. Concerning those who are immersed once, rather than three times, in baptism

Likewise, from the Apostolic Canons, c. 50.

[Note: Burchard, Book 4, c. 23; Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, c. 58; *Decretum*, Part 1, c. 128.]

If any presbyter or bishop does not celebrate the triple immersion of the one mystery [Note: [Col. 1825] “has celebrated.” — “he immerses”: Burchard], but immerses only once in baptism (which some command to be given into the Lord’s death [Note: [Col. 1825C] “Which is to be given”: the Prisca version differs from Gratian only at this point. For it reads: “which appears to be given into the Lord’s death,” and Burchard likewise. Ivo has: “which is commanded to be given into the Lord’s death” [“to give”: Ivo, *Panormia*]. The Greek is: *ἀλλὰ ἓν βάπτισμα τὸ εἰς τὸν θάνατον τοῦ κυρίου διδόμενον*, that is, “but one immersion, which is given into the Lord’s death.”), let him be deposed. For the Lord did not say to us, “Baptize into my death,” but [Note: [Col. 1825] Matthew 28:19]: “Go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.”

[Col. 1826A] **C. LXXX. On the same matter.** Likewise, Gregory to Leander, Bishop of the Spains, Book I, Epistle 41 [Note: [Col. 1825] Epistle 43 (written A.D. 591), Book I, Maurist edition.—Anselm, Book 9, chapter 61 (21). Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 60. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 130. *Polycarpus*, Book 3, title 10. Peter Lombard, same place.]

**Part XV.** Nothing truer can be answered concerning the triple immersion in baptism than what you yourselves have perceived: that, where faith is one, a differing custom does no harm to the holy Church. We, however, by immersing three times signify the mysteries of the three-day burial [Note: [Col. 1825] “make known”: the other collected editions except Argentinensis and Basiliensis], so that, when the infant is raised from the water for the third time, the resurrection after three days may be expressed [Note: [Col. 1825] “is expressed”: the same editions]. But if anyone perhaps thinks that this is also done in veneration of the supreme Trinity [Note: [Col. 1825] “judges”: the same editions except Basiliensis and Lyons II–III; the original; Ivo], this too does not prevent immersing those to be baptized once in the water; for, since there is one substance in three persons [Note: [Col. 1825] “substances”: Lyons II–III; “subsistences”: the remaining editions; Anselm; Ivo], it can in no way be reprehensible to immerse an infant in baptism either three times or once, since in three immersions the Trinity of persons, and in one the singularity of the Godhead [Note: [Col. 1825] “the Godhead singly”: Argentinensis; “the singularity of the Godhead”: Venetian editions I–II], may be signified.

**C. LXXXI. On the same matter.** Likewise, Jerome on the Epistle to the Ephesians, Book II, on chapter 4 [verse 5] [Note: [Col. 1826C] This chapter has been expanded and corrected from the original.] [Note: [Col. 1825] Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 61. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 131.]

In the same way, *also* [Note: [Col. 1825] The words enclosed in asterisks are not found in Ivo.] we are baptized *into* the Father [Note: [Col. 1825] “in the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit”: the other collected editions except Basiliensis], and *into* the Son, and *into* the Holy Spirit, and are immersed three times, so that the one sacrament of the Trinity may appear; *and we are not baptized in the names of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, but in one name, which is understood as God.* Likewise below, § 1. Baptism may also be called one in this sense: that, *although we are baptized three times* [Note: [Col. 1825] Add: “also”: Basiliensis] on account of the mystery of the Trinity, nevertheless it is reckoned one baptism [Note: [Col. 1825] “we baptize”: Ivo’s *Decretum*; “let him be baptized”: the other collected editions; Ivo’s *Panormia*.].

[Col. 1826C] **C. LXXXII. On those who immerse only once in the name of Christ.** Likewise, Pope Pelagius to Bishop Gaudentius [Note: [Col. 1825] Compare chapter 30 above.—Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 62. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 161.]

There are many who claim that they baptize solely in the name of Christ, and even with a single immersion. But the Gospel command, delivered by God himself and our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ [Note: [Col. 1825] “by the Lord and Savior himself”: Argentinensis and Basiliensis; “speaking and delivering”: Lyons II–III; “speaking or delivering”: the remaining editions except Basiliensis], admonishes us to confer holy baptism upon each person in the name of the Trinity, also with triple immersion, [Col. 1827A] the Lord saying to his disciples [Note: [Col. 1827] “the Lord Jesus Christ”: Argentinensis; “our Lord Jesus Christ”: the remaining editions; Ivo, *Panormia*] [Note: [Col. 1827] Matthew 28:19]: “Go, baptize all nations in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit” [Note: [Col. 1827C] “of the Holy Spirit”: here he seems to follow chapter *Si revera*, above in the same distinction].

**C. LXXXIII. At the invocation of the Trinity we must immerse three times in baptism.** Likewise, Pope Zacharias to Bishop Boniface, in the letter beginning, “At the sacred thresholds” [Note: [Col. 1827] Written A.D. 748.—Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 63. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 169. Peter Lombard, Book 4, distinction 3.]

**Part XVI.** In the synod of the English it is found to have been decreed, and judgment most firmly enjoined and carefully set forth [Note: [Col. 1827] Omitted by the other collected editions except Argentinensis and Basiliensis], that whoever had been immersed without invocation of the Trinity did not possess the sacrament of regeneration. This is altogether true; for if anyone has been washed [Note: [Col. 1827] “immersed”: the same editions; Ivo; the original] in the baptismal font without invocation of the Trinity, he is not a complete Christian [Col. 1827B] unless he has been baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. § 1. The priests also wished this to be observed [Note: [Col. 1827] “to have observed”: the original; “to observe”: Ivo, *Panormia*; the other collected editions except Lyons II–III] in the aforesaid synod [Note: [Col. 1827] Omitted from the original]: that if anyone did not name even one person of the Trinity in baptism [Note: [Col. 1827] “has not named”: Basiliensis], that baptism could not be true. This is certainly true, because one who has not confessed one person of the Holy Trinity cannot be a complete Christian. For one who confesses the Father and the Son, if he has not also confessed the Holy Spirit, has neither the Father nor the Son; and one who has confessed the Father and the Holy Spirit but has not confessed the Son has neither the Father nor the Holy Spirit, but is empty of divine grace [Note: [Col. 1827] “one”: Ivo; “let the name have been confessed”: the other collected editions].

[Col. 1827C] **C. LXXXIV. Those who have not been baptized in the name of the Trinity are to be rebaptized.** Likewise, Gregory to Quirinus [Note: [Col. 1827] Epistle 67 (written A.D. 601), Book 11, Maurist edition.—Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 64. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 153], Bishop in Iberia [Note: [Col. 1827] “Hibernia”: the other collected editions; Ivo; compare the correction to chapter 44 above in the same distinction], Book IX, Epistle 61.

But these heretics who are in no way baptized in the name of the Trinity [Note: [Col. 1827] “who do not baptize”: Basiliensis and Lyons; “who are not baptized”: the remaining editions; the word “in no way” is absent from Ivo’s *Decretum*], such as the Bonosians [Note: [Col. 1827] “Bonosiacs”: the original; Ivo’s *Decretum*] and the Cataphrygians [Col. 1828A] (for the former do not believe Christ to be the Lord, while the latter perversely believe the Holy Spirit to be a certain wicked man, Montanus; and there are many like them) [Note: [Col. 1827] “there are others, when”: the original; Ivo; Venetian I–II; “and there are such persons”: Argentinensis; “there are others of that kind, when”: the remaining editions], and others of that sort, are baptized when they come to the holy Church [Note: [Col. 1827] “let them be baptized”: Basiliensis and Lyons], because that was not baptism which, while they were in error, they did not receive in the name of the Holy Trinity [Note: [Col. 1827] The word “in” is absent from Ivo’s *Panormia*; “the Holy Trinity” is absent from Norimberg].

**C. LXXXV. It is permitted to immerse once in baptism.** Likewise, from the Fourth Council of Toledo, chapter 5 [Note: [Col. 1827] Held A.D. 633.—Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 59. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 129.]

To avoid the scandal of schism or the practice of heretical doctrine, let us maintain a single immersion in baptism.

**C. LXXXVI. On a priest who, through ignorance of the Latin language, erred in the invocation of the Trinity.** Likewise, Pope Zacharias to Bishop Boniface, in a decretal letter [Note: [Col. 1827] Written A.D. 744.—Burchard, Book 4, chapter 43. Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 65. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 237.]

[Col. 1828B] Your messengers reported [Note: [Col. 1827C] “Your messengers”: these two words seem to have been added by Gratian [though they are found in Ivo’s *Panormia*], so that he would not be obliged to recount what precedes in the letter; Burchard and Ivo nevertheless did so [Col. 1828C]. Although Virgil and Sidonius, who reported this, were not properly Boniface’s messengers.] that there was in that province a priest who was wholly ignorant of the Latin language; and when baptizing, not knowing how to speak Latin [Note: [Col. 1827] “Latin speech”: Ivo’s *Panormia* and the other collected editions], mangling the language, he said: “I baptize you in the name of the Fatherland [*Patria*], and of the Daughter [*Filia*], and of the Holy Spirit [*Spiritu sancta*]” [Note: [Col. 1827] “of the Fatherlands and Daughters and Holy Spirits”: Basiliensis; “of the Spirit”: the other collected editions except Burchard]. And for this reason your reverend brotherhood [Note: [Col. 1827] “holiness”: the other collected editions] considered rebaptizing them. But, most holy brother, if the one who baptized did so, as we have said above, not by introducing an error or heresy, but solely through ignorance of Roman speech and by mangling the language, we cannot agree that they should be baptized anew [Note: [Col. 1827] “as we stated above”: the same editions].

**C. LXXXVII. Why those baptized are anointed by a priest.** Likewise, Ambrose, *On the Sacraments*, treatise or Book I, chapter 2 [Note: [Col. 1827] This is not by Ambrose.—Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 51. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 109.]

[Col. 1828C] **Part XVII.** You came [Note: [Col. 1827] “We came”: the original] to the font; you entered it. Consider what you saw; consider what you said; recall it carefully. A Levite met you; a priest met you. You were anointed as an athlete of Christ [Note: [Col. 1827] “of God”: the other collected editions], so that you might approach baptism as a catechumen [Note: [Col. 1828C] “So that you might approach baptism”: Ivo likewise has this, and the author of the gloss at the word “Anointed” seems to have referred to it; but this entire clause is absent from the original, which instead reads: “as one about to contend in the struggle of this age, you professed the contests of your struggle.”].

[Col. 1829A] **C. LXXXVIII. Why one baptized by a priest is anointed on the head.** Likewise, Rabanus, *On the Institution of Clerics*, Book I, chapter 28 [Note: [Col. 1829] Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 66. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 140.]

After the baptized person has come up [Note: [Col. 1829] “comes up”: the other collected editions] from the font, he is immediately signed on the head by the priest with sacred chrism, with prayer accompanying it, so that he may become a participant in Christ’s kingdom and may be called a Christian from Christ.

**C. LXXXIX. What is said by the priest over the baptized person.** Likewise, Ambrose, *On the Sacraments*, treatise or Book II, chapter 7 [Note: [Col. 1829] This is not by Ambrose.—Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 67. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 141.]

You emerged [Note: [Col. 1829] “You emerged three times”: Argentinensis; “you were immersed”: Ivo’s *Panormia*] [Note: [Col. 1829C] “You emerged”: thus in Ivo. The original has: “Therefore you were immersed,” with the same sense that the author of the gloss derives from the word “You emerged.” This use of the word in this sense is frequent in St. Ambrose [Col. 1830C].]: you came to the priest. What did he say to you? “God,” he says [Note: [Col. 1829] Add: “to you”: the other collected editions], “the almighty Father, who regenerated you from water and the Holy Spirit, and granted you [Note: [Col. 1829] Omitted by the other collected editions except Basiliensis and Lyons II–III] forgiveness of your sins [Note: [Col. 1829] “the forgiveness of your sins”: Ivo’s *Panormia* and the other collected editions], may himself anoint [Note: [Col. 1829] “anoint”: the other collected editions] you unto eternal life.” [Col. 1829B] See where you have been anointed [Note: [Col. 1829] “anointed”: the same editions except Basiliensis]: “unto eternal life,” he says.

**C. XC. Why ointment is placed on the head of the baptized person.** Likewise, in Book III, *On the Sacraments*, chapters 1 and 2 [Note: [Col. 1829] Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 68. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 142.]

You received [Note: [Col. 1829] “You receive”: Ivo; “behold, you receive”: Argentinensis; “you received”: Böhm; “you receive myrrh”: the original] the mystery, that is, ointment upon the head. Why upon the head? Because the understanding of a wise person is in his head [Note: [Col. 1829] Ecclesiastes 2:14]. And below, chapter 2: § 1. The spiritual seal follows [Note: [Col. 1829] “special”: Basiliensis], which you heard read today, because after the font [Note: [Col. 1829] “fonts”: the other collected editions] it remains for perfection to be effected, when the Holy Spirit is poured out at the priest’s invocation [Note: [Col. 1829] “so that”: the same editions; Ivo].

**C. XCI. Why a white garment is given to Christians.** Likewise, Rabanus, *On the Institution of Clerics*, Book I, chapter 29 [Note: [Col. 1829] Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 69. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 144.]

[Col. 1829C] After baptism a white garment is given to the Christian [Note: [Col. 1829] “to Christians”: the other collected editions], signifying [Note: [Col. 1829] “which signifies”: Argentinensis; “which means”: the remaining editions; Ivo] Christian innocence and purity, which, after the old stains have been washed away [Note: [Col. 1829] “removed”: Norimberg, Venetian I–II, Paris, Lyons I], he ought to preserve unspotted through the care of holy conduct, to be presented before Christ’s judgment seat [Note: [Col. 1829] “for presenting”: the original and Ivo’s *Decretum*; “for re-presenting”: *Panormia* and the other collected editions except Lyons II–III]. All who are born again are clothed in white garments for the mystery [Note: [Col. 1829] “ministry”: Norimberg and Paris; “holy”: Basiliensis and Lyons II–III] of the Church rising again. Likewise there: § 1. Therefore [Note: [Col. 1829] Omitted by Ivo] those baptized use white garments, so that those whose face at their first birth had been darkened by the rag of inveterate error may display the garment of the glory of their second birth [Note: [Col. 1829] “infancy”: the original]. [Col. 1830A] For after the sacred anointing his head is covered with a mystical veil, so that he may understand that he possesses the diadem of kingship and priestly dignity.

**C. XCII. On the same matter.** Likewise, Ambrose in the book *On Those Initiated into the Mysteries*, chapter 7 [Note: [Col. 1829] Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 70. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 144.]

After baptism you received white garments, so that it might be an indication that you had put off the covering [Note: [Col. 1829] “pleasure”: Argentinensis, Basiliensis, Paris, Lyons I; “pleasure” in the accusative: the remaining editions; Ivo’s *Panormia*] of sins and had put on the chaste coverings of innocence.

**C. XCIII. For how many months Jews are to be kept among the catechumens.** Likewise, from the Council of Agde, chapter 34 [Note: [Col. 1829] Held A.D. 506.—Burchard, Book 4, chapter 81. Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 71. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 275.]

**Part XVIII.** Jews, whose faithlessness frequently [Col. 1830B] returns to the vomit, if they wish to come to the Catholic law [Note: [Col. 1829] “Catholic laws”: the other collected editions], are to enter the threshold of the Church among the catechumens for eight months; and if they are known to come with pure faith, only then may they obtain the grace of baptism [Note: [Col. 1829] “may attain”: the same collection, though this is nevertheless a variant reading]. But if, by some chance, they incur the danger of illness within the prescribed period [Note: [Col. 1829] “if he incurs it—and is despaired of, let him be baptized”: the same collection], and are despaired of, let them be baptized.

**C. XCIV. On the many Jews who frequently return to Judaism.** Likewise, from the Fourth Council of Toledo, chapter 58 [Note: [Col. 1829] Held A.D. 633. Burchard, Book 1, chapter 85. Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 75. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 279.]

Many Jews who long ago were brought into the Christian faith are now known, while blaspheming Christ, not only to have practiced Jewish rites, but even to have presumed to perform abominable circumcisions. Concerning these, at the counsel [Note: [Col. 1829] “deliberately”: the Hispanic Collection; “it was resolved”: Ivo’s *Decretum*] of our most pious and religious lord King Sisemund [Note: [Col. 1829] “Sisenand”: the Hispanic Collection, Burchard, and Ivo’s *Panormia*; “Sisemund”: Ivo’s *Decretum*; the other collected editions except Argentinensis], this holy council decreed that transgressors of this kind, corrected by pontifical authority, should be recalled to the observance of Christian doctrine [Note: [Col. 1829] “to the dignity of Christianity”: the other collected editions], so that those whom their own will does not amend may be restrained by priestly punishment. Those whom they have circumcised [Note: [Col. 1829] “surrounded”: Basiliensis; “circumcise”: the other editions except Argentinensis], if they are their sons [Note: [Col. 1829] Omitted by Argentinensis], are to be separated from association with their parents; if slaves, they are to be granted freedom because of the injury to their bodies.

[Col. 1831A] **C. XCV. Before baptism we must renounce the devil and his works.** Likewise, Rabanus, *On the Institution of Clerics*, Book I, chapter 27 [Note: [Col. 1831] Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 76. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 78.]

The pagan is first asked [Note: [Col. 1831] “let him be asked”: the other collected editions; Ivo] whether he renounces the devil [Note: [Col. 1831] “all pomps” is added in Venetian I–II, Paris, and Lyons I; “and all pomps” in Lyons II–III] and all his harmful works and deceitful pomps [Note: [Col. 1831] “all”: Ivo and the other collected editions], so that he may first reject error and thus draw near to truth, and, in accordance with the Apostle [Note: [Col. 1831] Ephesians 4:22], may put off the old man according to his former manner of life, who is corrupted according to the desires of error, renouncing ungodliness and worldly desires.

**C. XCVI. One who does not repent of the old life does not pass into the new life.** Likewise, Augustine, in the book *On the Remedy of Penance*, chapter 2 [Note: [Col. 1831] Compare Distinction 1, *On Penance*, chapter 81.—Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 35. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 76.]

[Col. 1831B] Everyone who has now become master of his own will, when he approaches the sacraments of believers, cannot begin a new life unless he repents of his old life. Infants alone are exempt from this repentance when they are baptized; for they cannot yet use free choice [Note: [Col. 1831] “could”: Ivo’s *Panormia*].

**C. XCVII. We must do penance before baptism.** The same [Note: [Col. 1831] Epistle 265, Maurist edition, date uncertain.—Anselm, Book 11, chapter 1. Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 36. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 77. Peter Lombard, Book 4, distinction 16] to Seleuciana [Note: [Col. 1831] “Salernitanus”: Basiliensis; “Salactitanus”: Lyons; “Satectitanus”: the remaining editions], Epistle CVIII.

Before baptism people do penance for their former sins, but in such a way that they are also baptized, as is written in the Acts of the Apostles, where Peter speaks to the Jews and says [Note: [Col. 1831] Acts 2:38]: “Do penance, and let each one of you be baptized [Note: [Col. 1831] Omitted by Basiliensis] in the name [Note: [Col. 1831] “our” is added by Ivo’s *Panormia* and the other collected editions] of the Lord Jesus Christ.”

[Col. 1831C] **C. XCVIII. A forty-day abstinence is prescribed for Jews to be baptized.** Likewise, Gregory [Note: [Col. 1831] Epistle 23 (written A.D. 598), Book 8, Maurist edition.—Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 37. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 61] to Fantinus [Note: [Col. 1831] “Faustinus”: the other collected editions], Defensor, Book VII, Epistle 24.

Lest, God forbid, long delay should be able to turn the minds of the Jews back again, speak with our brother, the bishop of that place [Note: [Col. 1831] “of that place”: Ivo and the other collected editions], so that, after forty days of penance and abstinence have been prescribed, either on the Lord’s Day [Col. 1832A] or, if some particularly celebrated festival should happen to occur, protected by the mercy of almighty God, you may baptize them [Note: [Col. 1831] “let him baptize”: the original; Ivo’s *Decretum*].

**C. XCIX. Penance is not necessary for those being baptized.** Likewise, Ambrose on the Epistle to the Romans, on chapter 11 [Note: [Col. 1831] This is not by Ambrose.—Compare Gratian after Distinction 1, *On Penance*, chapter 87.]

“The gifts and calling of God are without repentance,” because the grace of God in baptism does not require groaning, does not require weeping or any work, but faith alone [Note: [Col. 1831C] “but faith alone”: thus in the Ordinary Gloss, from which Gratian seems more likely to have taken this passage than from Ambrose; Ambrose reads, “except only a profession from the heart,” as is also reported above, *On Penance*, Distinction 1, chapter *Quis aliquando*, at the word “The grace of God”], and freely forgives everything.

**C. C. When necessity compels, the same godparent may serve in catechism and confirmation.** Likewise, Pope Hyginus [Note: [Col. 1831] Taken from chapter 4 of Theodore in Petit.—Burchard, Book 4, chapter 24. Anselm, Book 9, chapter 25. Ivo, *Panormia*, Book 1, chapter 77. *Decretum*, Part 1, chapter 218.]
